title: Car Paint Visualizer with Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D car paint visualizer using Three.js. Load the model 'Corset.glb' using GLTFLoader from a CDN (use the Khronos glTF sample models CDN or local path). This model serves as the product showcase object (treat it as the displayable product in a paint/finish visualizer context).

## Scene Setup
- Initialize a Three.js scene with a dark gradient background (top: #1a1a2e, bottom: #16213e).
- Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.5, 3) looking at origin.
- Add OrbitControls with damping enabled (dampingFactor=0.05), autoRotate initially OFF.
- Add lighting: one DirectionalLight (intensity 1.5, position 5,5,5), one HemisphereLight (sky: #ffffff, ground: #444444, intensity 0.6), and one PointLight (color white, intensity 1.0, position -3, 2, -3).
- Load 'Corset.glb' model. Center it at origin. Scale it so it fits within a 2-unit bounding sphere. Store reference to the model.
- Create a reflective floor plane (CircleGeometry radius 3, MeshStandardMaterial with metalness 0.9, roughness 0.1, color #111111) at y=-0.5.

## Paint System
- Define 6 paint colors with names and hex values:
  1. 'Midnight Black' (#0a0a0a)
  2. 'Racing Red' (#cc0000)
  3. 'Ocean Blue' (#0044aa)
  4. 'Pearl White' (#f0f0f0)
  5. 'Forest Green' (#006633)
  6. 'Sunset Orange' (#ff6600)
- Each paint has associated metalness and roughness: Black(0.8,0.2), Red(0.7,0.3), Blue(0.6,0.25), White(0.5,0.4), Green(0.65,0.3), Orange(0.55,0.35).
- Default paint is index 0 (Midnight Black).
- Apply paint by traversing all mesh children of the loaded model and setting their material to a new MeshStandardMaterial with the paint color, metalness, roughness, and envMapIntensity=1.0.

## Particle System
- Create a particle system with 500 particles using BufferGeometry and PointsMaterial (size 0.03, transparent, opacity 0.7).
- Particles should orbit around the model in a toroidal pattern.
- Each particle has a random angle, radius (between 1.0 and 2.0), height offset (-0.5 to 0.5), and speed.
- Particles should be colored to match the current paint color.
- Particle animation: each frame, update particle positions by incrementing their angle by their speed * deltaTime.
- Add a toggle to enable/disable particles (default: enabled).
- Track particle count that are currently visible.

## UI Controls (DOM overlay)
- Create a top-left HUD panel showing: current paint name, metalness, roughness, particle count, FPS.
- Create a bottom color picker bar: 6 circular buttons (50px each) with the paint colors, arranged horizontally centered. Each button has a 3px white border; the active one gets a 3px gold (#ffd700) border.
- Add a 'Toggle Particles' button (top-right corner).
- Add a 'Toggle Auto-Rotate' button below the particle toggle.
- Add a 'Reset Camera' button below auto-rotate toggle.
- Add a 'Toggle Wireframe' button below reset camera.

## Keyboard Controls
- Keys 1-6: Select paint colors (1=Black, 2=Red, 3=Blue, 4=White, 5=Green, 6=Orange).
- Key 'P': Toggle particles on/off.
- Key 'R': Reset camera to initial position.
- Key 'A': Toggle auto-rotate.
- Key 'W': Toggle wireframe mode on the model.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ object updated every frame with:
- modelLoaded: boolean (true once GLB is loaded)
- currentPaintIndex: number (0-5)
- currentPaintName: string
- currentColor: hex string (e.g., '#cc0000')
- metalness: number
- roughness: number
- particlesEnabled: boolean
- particleCount: number (500 when enabled, 0 when disabled)
- autoRotate: boolean
- wireframeMode: boolean
- cameraDistance: number (distance from camera to origin)
- cameraPosition: {x, y, z} (rounded to 2 decimals)
- fps: number (current frames per second)
- modelScale: number (uniform scale applied to model)
- floorVisible: boolean (always true)
- paintChanges: number (count of how many times paint was changed, starts at 0)
- envMapIntensity: number

## Animation Loop
- Use requestAnimationFrame.
- Update OrbitControls.
- Animate particles.
- Calculate and display FPS.
- Update __3D_STATE__ every frame.

Ensure the page is fully self-contained with all dependencies loaded from CDN (three.js r158+, OrbitControls, GLTFLoader).
physics_constraints: Particles must follow toroidal orbital paths around the model. Camera distance must remain positive and finite. All material values (metalness, roughness) must stay within [0,1] range. Particle positions must be NaN-free and bounded within radius 3 of origin.
